If your working directory is myfolder/homework/, what relative path would you specify to get the file located at myfolder/MyData.csv?
Since the file we want is only one folder above the current working directory, we can simply specify ../MyData.csv as the relative file path. The ../ path prefix points to one folder above the current working directory.
What are the major benefits of using R projects?
R projects support the use of working directories and version control software. Working directories establish relative paths, which eliminate the need for each user to hard-code file paths specific to their machine. Relative paths are very helpful for code sharing, and version control is also helpful for code sharing. Through an R project for version control we can clone a Git repository and manage that repository through R Studio’s terminal.
What is Git and what is GitHub?
Git a type of version control software. GitHub is an online platform for hosting and sharing Git-based projects (the actual version control actions still happen within Git).
What are the two main differences between a tibble and a data.frame?

Fancy print. A data frame prints in its entirety vs. a tibble prints the first few rows of data and a size summary (#rows x #cols).
Limited type coercion. A single column of a tibble can be accessed by [ without coercing to a vector.

title: ST558_HW3_Will
text:
If your working directory is myfolder/homework/, what relative path would you specify to get the file located at myfolder/MyData.csv?
You would need to specify ‘../MyData.csv’ as this is located one level up from the working directory.
What are the major benefits of using R projects?
The working directory for R projects is set to the project’s root folder. This makes it easy for when you have multiple users working on the project due to the relative file paths being consistent between machines. Pathing does not break between machines. Related files are self contained.
What is Git and what is GitHub?
Git is a software that tracks files, changes to those files, allows you to branch to silo work and merge code changes safely. Github is a cloud hosting platform for git repos with some additional tooling for tracking, approvals, permissions policies, etc.
What are the two main differences between a tibble and a data.frame?
Printing a tibble only prints the first several rows whereas printing a data.frame will print all rows of that object. They differ in subsetting. Tibble does not allow for partial matching on column names with ‘$’ whereas a data.frame can partially match a column name.

If your working directory is myfolder/homework/, what relative path would you specify to get the file located at myfolder/MyData.csv?
We can use ../MyData.csv, typically inside a read.csv() function. The .. prefix means we go up one level from our current working directory, putting us inside myfolder
What are the major benefits of using R projects?
When an R project is created, it gets associated with a directory (folder or repo) and uses this as the projects working directory. This is very useful, because if we have this repo shared (via Github), other users can pick up the same R project and all the paths should work. This allows for organization and seamless collaboration.
What is Git and what is GitHub?
Git is the actual software that performs version contolling. whereas Github is the online hosting service for projects that utilize Git software. Version controlling allows us to save every change that occurs in our project folder, and revert back to previous saves.
What are the two main differences between a tibble and a dataframe?
Tibbles are a modern re-imagining of the data frame. When printing a tibble, we only see the first few rows/columns, whereas printing a dataframe prints everything to the console. Tibbles also force you to confront problems earlier when subsetting, as they dont do partial matching. df$colnam on a dataframe will match a column named colname, whereas with a tibble it warns you explicitly the column doesn’t exist

getIQR <- function(vector, ...) { # ... Allows other unnamed arguments to be passed

  return(q[2] - q[1])
}

text:
If your working directory is myfolder/homework/, what relative path would you specify to get the file located at myfolder/MyData.csv?
You would need to specify ‘../MyData.csv’ as this is located one level up from the working directory. The ‘../’ prefix moves you up one level from current into ‘myfolder/’ where ‘MyData.csv’ lives.
What are the major benefits of using R projects?
The working directory for R projects is set to the project’s root folder. Relative file paths stay consistent no matter whose machine is being used for the project. This makes collaboration more seamless without paths breaking. Relative paths are very helpful for code sharing, and version control is also helpful for code sharing. Through an R project for version control we can clone a Git repository and manage that repository through R Studio’s terminal. Related files are self contained.
What is Git and what is GitHub?
Git is a software that tracks files, changes to those files, allows you to branch to silo work and merge code changes safely. Github is a cloud hosting platform for git repos with some additional tooling for tracking, approvals, permissions policies, etc.
What are the two main differences between a tibble and a data.frame?
Printing a tibble only prints the first several rows and size summary (#rows x #cols), whereas printing a data.frame will print all rows of that object. They differ in subsetting. Tibble does not allow for partial matching on column names with ‘$’ whereas a data.frame can partially match a column name.

Task 4: Writing a function

8.
We are going to write a function to get the interquartile range of a vector, we use names = F to remove the percentages names. And add ... to allow unamed arguments for the quantile function.

getIQR <- function(v, ...){
  
  quantile(v, names = F, ...)[4] - quantile(v, names = F, ...)[2]
  
  
}



9.
Now, we are going to apply the getIQR() function to the fixed_acidity,

getIQR(wine_data$fixed_acidity)

[1] 1.3


and the citric_acid columns.

getIQR(wine_data$citric_acid)

[1] 0.14




10.
We are going to write a function to get the coefficient of variation

getCoefVar <- function(v, ...){
  
  sd(v, ...) / abs(mean(v, ...))
  
}



11.
And we apply to the fixed_acidity column,

getCoefVar(wine_data$fixed_acidity)

[1] 0.1796783


and to the citric_acid column.

12.
We need to create a wrapper function that return the IQR and the coefficient of variation for a given vector. The output is a list with both of the values calculated.

getSummaries <- function(v, ...){
  
  list(IQR = getIQR(v, ...), Coef_Var = getCoefVar(v, ...))
  
}
